title: Position Group or Draft Class
description: Preserves class depth, tiers, archetypes, scarcity and strategic implications for a position group.
principles: Preserve the group-level thesis independently of individual player profiles.
Keep talent depth, role depth, draft capital and market scarcity distinct.
Complete rankings and tiers must be represented when safely reconstructable.
Format-dependent positional value must remain explicit.

dimensions.description: Depth and quality distribution across the group.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve where confidence drops and why.
detection_questions: How many clear targets or starters does the source see?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Retain tier membership, order certainty and unclear boundaries.
detection_questions: Is order inside a tier firm?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve archetypes and their fantasy relevance.
detection_questions: What types of players exist in the group?

dimensions.description: Balance between prospect quality and landing spot.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Keep talent and opportunity arguments separate.
detection_questions: Is the group weak in talent, situation or both?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve how draft capital changes confidence.
detection_questions: How does the source use draft capital?

dimensions.description: Common routes to snaps or opportunity.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Retain recurring role mechanisms across the group.
detection_questions: What gets these players on the field?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Explain how scarcity changes draft price without equating it to talent.
detection_questions: Are players pushed up because alternatives disappear?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve specialist value and format-specific changes.
detection_questions: Does PPR, return scoring, TE premium or another rule change the group?
What can cause the class or tier to disappoint?

passing: Preserve the reference only where it is needed to understand another argument.
Do not create an artificial standalone evaluation.
brief: Preserve the conclusion and its immediate qualifier or condition.
Do not expand beyond what the source supports.
substantive: Preserve the conclusion plus the meaningful reason, condition, risk or uncertainty supplied by the source.
Keep format, price or time-horizon distinctions when they materially change the view.
deep: Preserve the complete major reasoning chain rather than only the final verdict.
Represent every materially discussed dimension, including competing positive and negative cases.
Keep disagreements, uncertainty, conditions and failure paths.
structural: Preserve the broad thesis, its mechanism, its scope and the subjects it affects.
Create independently reusable context takes rather than burying the thesis inside one player.

review_questions: Is the group-level conclusion preserved in addition to player takes?
Are tier breaks and ordering uncertainty clear?
Is positional scarcity distinguished from player quality?
Are shared role paths and risks represented?
forbidden_distortions: Do not infer a complete order when the source only provides tiers.
Do not treat market scarcity as proof of talent.
Do not omit the group thesis after producing individual player takes.
Do not flatten format-specific specialist value.
extension_signals: A new position-specific dimension repeatedly matters.
A draft-class episode uses a structure not covered by rankings or tiers.
A scoring format creates a new group-level evaluation category.
The profile cannot represent class-level uncertainty.
